newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: The South African rand drifted to a slightly stronger close on Monday as players searched the horizon for a signal to break from its near-term range.
"It's just following that (dollar)mark rate and not much else. I expect tomorrow will be much of the same," said one dealer.
Another said: "I'm not sure what's going to get us going either way tomorrow, possibly PPI, but that's more for the debt punters. I think all this good weather has made our market drowsy."
South Africa's Producer Price Index for June will be unveiled by the Central Statistical Service on Tuesday.
Economists have forecast the index as rising 8.3 percent year-on-year or 0.5 percent month-on-month in June from 8.4 and 0.9 percent in May
The rand was last quoted at 4.6665/6695 to the dollar from Friday's late level of 4.6710/6740.
Dealers said exporter demand and London-based dollar sales helped the rand out after it pushed through 4.67 around midday.
A likely range of 4.66-4.68 was marked out for Tuesday, barring any massive overnight swings by the dollar.
In cross rate trading the rand was last trading at 0.3979/3983 on the mark from 0.3966/3969 Friday and at 24.9026/9293 yen from 24.8394/8768.
Against sterling, the rand last traded at 7.4175/4269 from Friday's late 7.3505/3599 level.
Bonds closed in positive territory after an unsteady session governed by uncertainty about just how much action related to last week's options close-out was left to filter through the market.
Yields for the benchmark R150 long bond pushed up early but found 14.30 percent too strong.
It closed at 14.22 percent from a pre-weekend finish of 14.23 percent as solid foreign buying came in as well as local jobbers scurrying to cover shorts.

"You had a lot of people wondering to what extent the market was called at the (14.00 percent) big figure. In the end though, I don't think too many were game to write fresh shorts above 14.30 percent," said one Johannesburg-based dealer.
Offered rates for three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.40 to 15.50 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was 14.90 to 14.95 percent.

The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage fell to 8.83 billion rand on Friday after rising to 9.031 billion rand on Thursday. There was no shortage figure fro Saturday due to the Women's Day national public holiday.
Foreigners bought a hefty 834.37 million rands worth of South African bonds on Friday after selling a net 29.29 million rands on Thursday, the Bond Exchange said.
Turnover was 13.02 billion rand on Friday from 71.1 billion rand on Thursday which was a settlement day and the exchange's biggest day on record in turnover terms.
